spiral galaxies originate from the cold gas inflows from cosmic webs, and their morphologies are determined by the amount of gas inflow and by the amount of the hot gas surrounding the galaxy.
the mass-dependent structures of galaxies are reproduced by a unified theory based on the cold-flow scenario.
spiral galaxies with various masses can be explained in terms of the cold gas inflows from cosmic webs.

a unified formation scenario of spiral galaxies that explains the mass-dependent structures and the chemical properties of their discs.
the origin of the morphological variety of the spiral galaxies.
a new paradigm for the formation of spiral galaxies in which cold accretion is responsible for the formation of thin discs and bulges, and cooling flow is for thick discs.

the morphological diversity of spiral galaxy is a consequence of a unified formation scenario of cold accretion and cooling flow.
the cold accreting gas is responsible for the formation of spiral galaxies with a wide range of morphologies.
the morphological diversity of spiral galaxy is a natural outcome of their growth history.

the cold-flow hypothesis can explain the formation of spiral galaxy structure in a self-consistent manner.
the cold accertion creates a thick disc and bulge, whereas the cooling flow forms a thin disc.
the cold-flow hypothesis provides a natural and unified explanation for the mass-dependence of the morphological diversity of spiral and elliptical galaxies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the morphological diversity of spiral galaxy can be understood in terms of the cold accretions from cosmic web and the subsequent evolution of the accreted gas.
the cold accreting gas forms a thick disc and the cooling flow gas forms a thin disc and bulge.
the mass dependence of spiral galaxy structures can be understood by a single formation process of cold gas accretion from the cosmic web.
